summary: This reader has an undergraduate computer science degree: discrete mathematics (modular arithmetic, gcd and primes, binomial counting, induction), linear algebra over the reals and small fields (subspaces, rank, elimination, eigenvalues, dot-product orthogonal complements and projections), and algorithms (divide-and-conquer recurrences, Karatsuba multiplication, and the DFT and cyclic convolution as used for FFT-based polynomial multiplication). Complex numbers are known as far as roots of unity and Gaussian integers, Turing machines are known with multiple tapes, and basic probability reaches the union bound. Tensor products, bilinear forms beyond the dot product, quotient rings and the sources' network and address constructions are not part of this background.

known.name: Vector spaces, subspaces, bases and dimension
known.gloss: A set closed under addition and scalar multiplication over a field, whose subspaces, bases and dimension are the usual notions of linear algebra.

known.name: Rank of a matrix
known.gloss: The number of linearly independent rows or columns of a matrix, equal to the dimension of its column space.

known.name: Invertible matrices and inverses
known.gloss: A square matrix M is invertible when some matrix M^-1 satisfies M M^-1 = I, and then M represents a bijective linear map.

known.name: Gaussian elimination and triangular matrices
known.gloss: Row reduction by elementary row operations, which puts a matrix in echelon form, and matrices whose entries vanish on one side of the diagonal.

known.name: Eigenvalues and diagonalization
known.gloss: A scalar lambda is an eigenvalue of a matrix A when Av = lambda v for some nonzero vector v, and a matrix is diagonalizable when it is similar to a diagonal matrix.

known.name: Dot product, orthogonal complement and projection
known.gloss: The dot product of two vectors, the set of vectors orthogonal to every vector of a subspace, and the linear map that projects onto a subspace along a complementary subspace.

known.name: Permutations and permutation matrices
known.gloss: A permutation is a bijection of a finite index set to itself, and its permutation matrix is the 0-1 matrix that moves coordinates accordingly.

known.name: Modular arithmetic
known.gloss: Integers a and b are congruent modulo q when q divides a minus b, and arithmetic on the residue classes Z/qZ is well defined.

known.name: Greatest common divisor and coprimality
known.gloss: The greatest common divisor of two integers is the largest integer dividing both, computable by Euclid's algorithm, and two integers are coprime when their gcd is 1.

known.name: Prime numbers
known.gloss: A prime is an integer greater than 1 whose only positive divisors are 1 and itself, and every integer greater than 1 factors uniquely into primes.

known.name: Chinese remainder theorem
aliases: Chinese remainder theorem for coprime moduli
known.gloss: For pairwise coprime moduli q_1, ..., q_k, the system of congruences x = a_i modulo q_i has a unique solution modulo their product.

known.name: Binary field GF(2)
known.gloss: The field with two elements 0 and 1, in which addition is exclusive or (XOR) and multiplication is AND.

known.name: Hamming weight
known.gloss: The Hamming weight of a binary vector is its number of entries equal to 1.

known.name: Indicator vector of a set
known.gloss: The 0-1 vector of a finite set with entry 1 exactly at the elements of the set, given a fixed ordering of the ground set.

known.name: Binomial coefficients
known.gloss: The binomial coefficient C(n, k) is the number of k-element subsets of an n-element set.

known.name: Positional and mixed-radix notation
known.gloss: A representation of an integer as digits whose place values are powers of a fixed radix, or of a sequence of radices in the mixed-radix case.

known.name: Dyadic rationals
known.gloss: Rational numbers whose denominator is a power of two, equivalently the numbers with finitely many binary digits after the point.

known.name: Gaussian integers
known.gloss: The complex numbers a + bi with integers a and b, which form a ring under complex addition and multiplication.

known.name: Roots of unity
known.gloss: A complex number z is an nth root of unity when z^n = 1, and a primitive nth root has order exactly n, so its powers give all nth roots of unity.

known.name: Mathematical induction
known.gloss: A proof method that establishes a statement for every integer from a base case and a proof that each case implies the next.

known.name: Recurrence relations and geometric sums
known.gloss: An equation that defines a sequence in terms of its earlier terms, solved by unrolling it, together with the geometric sum of powers of a fixed ratio.

known.name: Iterated logarithm
known.gloss: The function log* n is the number of times the base-2 logarithm must be applied to n before the result is at most 1.

known.name: Logarithms, floor and ceiling
known.gloss: The base-2 logarithm, written lg n or log2 n, with the floor and ceiling functions that round it to integers.

known.name: Union bound
known.gloss: The probability that at least one of finitely many events occurs is at most the sum of the probabilities of the events.

known.name: Karatsuba multiplication
known.gloss: The divide-and-conquer multiplication of two n-bit integers that splits each into halves and uses three half-size products, running in O(n^1.585) time.
